title: Dedicated rollouts: add approve/abort endpoints + emit audit-style event log
author: Benji Okafor
body:
Context: Dedicated staged rollouts need explicit operator-controlled approvals per stage and an auditable record of every action. This PR adds control-plane endpoints to approve/abort a rollout stage, and emits structured audit-style events for both manual actions (approve/abort) and system actions (auto-hold) when invoked via the same surface. This follows the approvals/audit design in ADR-028 and unblocks Console workflows.

What’s included: Adds POST endpoints for approve and abort against a RolloutPlan execution (scoped to dedicated pool + rollout id), including request validation, idempotency, optimistic concurrency (plan_version), and permission checks. Adds event log emission for rollout actions using the existing audit export pipeline (actor, tenant_id, pool_id, rollout_id, stage_id, plan_version, request_id, reason). Adds unit tests for permission enforcement (internal operator vs enterprise tenant scopes) and idempotency behavior.

API surface (control plane): POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}:approve (body: {stage_id, plan_version, comment?, request_id?}); POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}:abort (body: {reason, plan_version, comment?, request_id?}). Both endpoints return the updated rollout execution summary (current_stage, state, last_event_at, plan_version).

Audit/event log: Emits structured events on success: rollout.approve, rollout.abort, rollout.auto_hold. Emission is best-effort but failures are surfaced to the caller (we fail the request if we cannot persist the event to the control-plane event log, to avoid un-audited state changes). We include a stable event_id derived from request_id (if present) to support de-dupe in downstream export.

RBAC: Requires rollout.approve to approve and rollout.abort to abort. Enterprise tenants are additionally scoped to their tenant_id and can only operate on pools they own. Internal operators can act across tenants when granted the operator scope.

Testing: Adds unit tests around (1) permission denied paths, (2) abort/approve idempotency with same request_id, (3) plan_version conflict returns 409, (4) audit event payload fields, and (5) cross-tenant access denied.

Notes/limitations: This PR does not implement automatic stage advancement; it only records approvals/aborts and emits events. Console and evaluator will build on these primitives. Auto-hold emission is plumbed through the same event writer but the evaluator integration will come in a separate PR.

Rollout safety: Approve is rejected when the rollout is not in HOLD state for the specified stage. Abort is allowed from HOLD/RUNNING and transitions the rollout to ABORTED with a required reason.

Docs: Inline endpoint comments reference the staged rollouts operator docs update in redwood-docs (tracked separately).

Follow-ups: Add pagination to the event log read endpoint (ENG-5122 follow-up), and extend audit event schema to include gate evaluation summary once evaluator lands (ENG-5124).
commits: rbac: enforce rollout.approve/rollout.abort permissions for dedicated rollouts
audit: emit rollout action events (approve/abort/auto_hold) with request_id de-dupe
tests: unit tests for permissions, version conflicts, and idempotency
checks: Build (bazel): PASS; Unit tests: PASS; Lint/Format: PASS (reran after fixing gofmt); API compatibility: PASS; Security policy checks: PASS
review_conversation: Ethan Park: Can we make sure approve only works when we’re explicitly held on that stage? Otherwise Console could accidentally advance through racey state. Also please call out behavior when plan_version mismatches.
Benji Okafor: Added state guard: approve requires HOLD on matching stage_id; otherwise 409 with current state/stage. Also added explicit 409 for plan_version conflict and tests.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC looks good, but the enterprise scope check should be done before we even fetch rollout details where possible. Also request_id should be required for idempotent retries from Console.

Benji Okafor: Moved tenant/pool ownership check to the route-level authz gate (before store read). For request_id: kept optional for now (CLI/manual calls), but if absent we generate one and return it; idempotency is only guaranteed when caller provides request_id. Documented in proto comments.

Marcus Lin: For auditability, we should not allow state transitions without a persisted event. Please confirm we fail closed if event write fails. Also ensure actor metadata includes auth subject + role.

Benji Okafor: Confirmed: approve/abort writes event in same control-plane transaction boundary (rollout update + event append). If event append fails, the whole operation fails. Actor now includes subject, auth_type, role, and impersonation flags.
Chloe Martin: Console needs a stable event id and a human-readable reason/comment. Please keep comment optional but preserve it in event payload. Also can we return last_event_at for UI polling?
Benji Okafor: Added event_id (derived from request_id hash) + optional comment + reason fields. Response now includes last_event_at and current plan_version.
Ethan Park: Approved after changes. Make sure we link this PR from ENG-5122 and note the idempotency semantics in the endpoint comments.
Benji Okafor: Linked ENG-5122 and updated comments. Thanks all.
release_notes: Internal: Dedicated staged rollouts now support approve/abort actions via control-plane API, with audit-style event log emission and RBAC enforcement. (Feature remains gated behind dedicated staged rollouts flag.)
